questions.question_text: A computer costs $\$800$ before GST. Find the price including GST.

options.why: Added $\$8$ instead of $10\%$ of $\$800$, which is $\$80$.
Subtracted the GST instead of adding it to the pre-GST price.
Divided by $1.1$ as if $\$800$ already included GST.

questions.question_text: A lounge costs $\$990$ including GST. Find the pre-GST price.

options.why: Took $10\%$ off $\$990$ instead of dividing by $1.1$; the base is not the inclusive price.
Added $10\%$ to $\$990$ instead of removing the GST already included.
Found the GST amount ($\$990 \div 11$) rather than the pre-GST price.

questions.question_text: A sign printer buys a roll of vinyl for $\$150$ and sells the finished signs for $\$186$. Find the percentage profit.

options.why: Divided the $\$36$ profit by the selling price instead of the cost price.
Divided the cost price by the selling price rather than using the profit.
Called the change a loss even though the selling price is higher than the cost.

questions.question_text: A caterer buys a coffee machine for $\$2500$ and later sells it for $\$1950$. Find the percentage profit or loss.

options.why: Divided the $\$550$ loss by the selling price instead of the cost price.
Ignored that the selling price is lower than the cost, so it is a loss.
Used $\$550$ as a percentage of the two prices added together, not of the cost price.

questions.question_text: A tool supplier makes a $30\%$ profit selling a drill for $\$286$. What did the supplier pay for the drill?

options.why: Took $30\%$ off $\$286$ instead of dividing by $130\%$; the selling price is not $100\%$.
Added $30\%$ to $\$286$ instead of working back to the cost price.
Found $30\%$ of $\$286$, the profit, rather than the cost price.

questions.question_text: A landscaper has two quotes for turf. Quote A is $\$1840$ before GST. Quote B is $\$2035$ including GST. Which quote is cheaper?

options.text: Quote A, by $\$11$, since it comes to $\$2024$ including GST.
Quote A, by $\$195$, comparing $\$1840$ with $\$2035$ directly.
options.why: Compares a pre-GST price with a GST-inclusive price without adding GST to Quote A.

options.text: Quote B, by $\$8.50$, since taking $10\%$ off Quote B gives $\$1831.50$.
options.why: Took $10\%$ off the GST-inclusive price instead of dividing by $1.1$, so the GST is stripped wrongly.

options.text: They cost the same once GST is added to both.
options.why: Only Quote A needs GST added; Quote B already includes it.

questions.solution_text:
Quote A, including GST: $\$1840 \times 1.1 = \$2024$.
Quote B, including GST: $\$2035$.
$\$2035 - \$2024 = \$11$
Quote A is cheaper by $\$11$.
